options.text: Filtration through the fine cloth can remove the remaining solid particles.
Decanting alone will always remove every fine particle that keeps the water cloudy.
When particles stay suspended after settling, filtration is needed rather than decanting alone.
A cloth with pores larger than the fine particles will still trap those particles.

stem:
Inaya has muddy water. After standing, some mud settles, but fine particles still make the water cloudy. She can pour off (decant) the upper liquid or filter it through a fine cloth. The cloth has small pores.

Which claims are correct? One or more options may be correct.

teacher.key_rationale: Fine suspended particles need filtration; decanting alone does not clear them, and pores must be smaller than the particles.
